cohort: 11,200,255 live births in 26 Brazilian state capitals and Brasilia between 1996 and 2011
finding: While the overall LBW rate remained stable, improvements in maternal education and antenatal care coverage were associated with a reduced risk of LBW in all regions of Brazil.
mod_finding: There was an increase in caesarean sections in all regions, with a small impact on LBW rates.
